title: The Scholar Who Forgot How to Swim (HI)
summary: An arrogant scholar mocks a simple boatman for not studying grammar and astronomy. When the boat leaks, the boatman asks a vital question. [HI]
full_text:
A proud scholar named Pandit Vidyadhar, who had spent forty years memorizing ancient texts of grammar, logic, and astronomy, hired a humble wooden ferry to cross the wide, turbulent river Yamuna during the monsoon.

As the boatman rowed with steady strokes, the scholar puffed his chest and asked: 'Boatman! Have you ever studied the sacred rules of Sanskrit grammar?'

The boatman replied humbly: 'No, master, I cannot read.'

The scholar scoffed: 'Alas! One-fourth of your entire life is completely wasted!'

A few minutes later, the scholar pointed to the sky: 'Boatman! Do you understand the planetary motions of Mars and Saturn and the science of astronomy?'

'No, master, I know only the river currents.'

The scholar shook his head: 'Tragic! Half of your entire life has been wasted in ignorance!'

Presently, the scholar asked: 'Do you know the twelve schools of Greek and Persian philosophy?'

'No, master, I know only how to row.'

'Hopeless!' the scholar declared. 'Three-fourths of your life is completely wasted!'

Just then, a sudden violent gale blew down the river. The small wooden ferry struck a submerged rock; water gushed into the hold, and the boat began to sink rapidly in the swirling, deep waves!

The boatman quickly took off his cotton tunic, turned to the trembling scholar, and asked:

'Master! Have you ever studied the art of swimming?'

The scholar screamed in terror, clutching the sinking gunwale: 'No! No! I never learned to swim! I studied only books!'

The boatman leaped into the water, shouting back:

'Alas, master! Then I fear your ENTIRE life is about to be wasted in the next two minutes!'

The boatman swam back, pulled the drowning scholar by the collar, and dragged him ashore, coughing water and shivering with cold.

Birbal, who had observed the rescue from the bank, helped the wet scholar up and said with a gentle smile:

'You see, Panditji? Book learning is splendid, but if you lack practical wisdom and humble skill, all the philosophy in the world cannot keep your head above water when the storms of life strike!'

The humbled scholar bowed to the boatman, cured forever of his intellectual arrogance.
